title: Each design option's picture shows that option's own difference
why: Your gripe, Oct 27 15:30 CDT (cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh2JEo4B1iU83SGsnRKwwcxZs, with a screenshot): on the Duo "Card in Hand" round 2 question, options A (Claim filed and Lost buttons) and B (the six existing stamps) carried the same generic title-card picture, so neither showed what was being decided.
note: d9 (in the c126/d9 lane) already requires a picture per option, scaled to the element being decided; it does not stop the same picture on every option. Fix: the waiting-page writer refuses a design item where two options share one image (same bytes or same file) or an image shows no element named in the item's focus; the item's focus names the state to draw (here, the late-package row with its buttons), and the skill tells the designer to draw that state per option. Red first on today's item. Needs no answer. Port: yes, the skill installs everywhere. Due after: c145 merges (same skill files; triage's waiting-page order, Oct 28: c145, c147, c122, c139, c135, c136). Placed ahead of c145 (triage, Oct 27): a gripe, and a picture that shows nothing makes the pick a guess. Green and reviewed: draft PR #753 (0b3ad80f), ready for batch 6. The page blocks Send when two options show the same picture with the same focus, or a focus finds no element. Review notes, not blocking: the check also runs on non-look decisions; the focus compare is a string compare; each check parses focused mockups again (cost unmeasured). Done: merged in batch 7 (PR #763, main a64166ae, Oct 28 06:47 CDT).
